chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'O Abu Hamza! The ablution before the meal and after it both remove poverty.' I said, 'May my father and my mother be sacrificed for you! They both remove poverty?' So he said: 'Yes, they both remove it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material benefit of performing ablution before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the spiritual and material efficacy of performing ablution before and after meals, linking physical purity with the removal of poverty (*al-faqar*). This practice is viewed in Shia tradition not merely as hygiene but as a means of attracting divine sustenance (*rizq*) by preparing the body and soul for nourishment, thereby preventing the spiritual and physical stagnation associated with poverty.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Safwan Al Jammal, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘O Abu Hamza! The ablution before the meal and after it both remove the poverty’. I said, ‘May my father and my mother be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! They both remove the poverty?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, they both remove it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Safwan al-Jammal from abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘O abu Hamzah, Wudu (washing) before and after eating food removes poverty.’ I then said, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, does it remove poverty?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it removes poverty.’”
